categories.heading: What can I customize?
categories.body: These are starting places — not limits.

items.title: EVENTS
items.body: Wedding décor, party favors, event pieces

items.title: JUST BECAUSE
items.body: If you have an idea, ask.

steps.title: Tell me your idea
steps.body: Share the details, inspiration, dimensions, colors, quantity — whatever you already know.

steps.title: We'll figure it out
steps.body: I review the request and determine materials, production method, and pricing that fit the piece.

steps.title: Approve your design
steps.body: For applicable custom pieces, you'll get a proof or mockup before production begins.

steps.title: I make it
steps.body: Once approved, the piece is made by hand and prepared for pickup or shipping.

items.q: How much do custom orders cost?
items.a: Custom pricing depends on size, materials, complexity, and quantity. I'll share an estimate after reviewing your idea.

items.q: How long do custom orders take?
items.a: Production time varies depending on the project and current workload. Please allow handmade processing time — and share your desired date in the form.

items.q: Can you work from an idea instead of a finished design?
items.a: Yes. Describe the idea and share inspiration or reference images. We can shape the details together.

items.q: Can you make something that isn't shown here?
items.a: Probably. If it fits the Wildhouse Lane studio (laser-cut, engraved, or handmade keepsakes), ask. The worst I can say is not this time.

form.heading: Start a custom order
form.intro: Tell me what you're imagining. I'll reply by email with next steps.
form.successMessage: Your email draft should open shortly — add any reference photos as attachments, then send when you're ready.
form.errorMessage: Please fill in your name, a valid email, what you want made, and a short description of your idea.
form.disclaimer: I understand that submitting this form is an inquiry and does not guarantee an order or final price.
form.uploadNote: File uploads aren't connected yet. After your email draft opens, attach inspiration photos there — or reply to my response with images.
